questions.question: Two point charges +3 μC and +5 μC are placed 2 m apart in vacuum. The magnitude of the electrostatic force between them is: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
A charge +2 μC is placed at the origin. The electric field intensity at point (3 m, 4 m) is: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
options: A) 720 N/C along the line joining origin to the point
B) 720 N/C perpendicular to the line joining origin to the point
C) 360 N/C perpendicular to the line
D) 360 N/C along the line joining origin to the point
questions.explanation: r = √(3²+4²) = 5 m. E = kq/r² = (9×10⁹)(2×10⁻⁶)/25 = 720 N/C along the radial direction (line joining origin to point).

questions.question: A uniform electric field E = 500 N/C exists in a region. A square surface of side 10 cm is placed such that the field makes an angle of 60° with the area vector. The electric flux through the surface is:
A solid insulating sphere of radius 5 cm carries +12 μC uniformly distributed throughout its volume. The electric field at a point 3 cm from the center is: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
Two charges +4q and -q are fixed at x = 0 and x = L respectively. A third charge q₀ placed on the x-axis experiences zero net force. The position of q₀ is:
questions.explanation: For equilibrium at x > L: k(4q)q₀/x² = k(q)q₀/(x-L)² → 4/x² = 1/(x-L)² → 2/x = 1/(x-L) → x = 2L.

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged to 100 V and disconnected from the battery. If the plate separation is doubled, the new potential difference is:
questions.explanation: Q constant, C = ε₀A/d. When d doubles, C halves. V = Q/C → V_new = Q/(C/2) = 2V = 200 V.

questions.question: A wire of resistance 10 Ω is stretched to double its length. The new resistance is (uniform cross-section, resistivity unchanged):
questions.explanation: Volume constant → area halves when length doubles. R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4ρL/A = 40 Ω.

questions.question: A circular coil (radius 10 cm, 100 turns, current 2 A) is placed in a 0.3 T field with its plane perpendicular to the field. The torque is:
questions.explanation: τ = mB sinθ. Plane perpendicular to B → area vector ∥ B (θ=0°) → τ = 0.

questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength (and highest frequency) in the EM spectrum.

questions.question: An electromagnetic wave has wavelength 600 nm. Its frequency is: (c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
The Poynting vector S = (1/μ₀)(E×B) represents:
options: B) Rate of energy flow per unit area
questions.explanation: S represents energy flux (power per unit area) carried by the EM wave.

questions.question: An EM wave of intensity 1000 W/m² is completely absorbed by a surface. The radiation pressure is: (c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
questions.explanation: For complete absorption: P = I/c = 1000/(3×10⁸) = 3.33×10⁻⁶ Pa.

questions.question: An EM wave propagates in +x direction with E = E₀sin(kx-ωt) along +y. The magnetic field is along:
questions.explanation: For wave in +x with E in +y, B must be in +z (E×B points along propagation). Both oscillate in phase.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. The image distance is:
In Young's double-slit experiment with λ = 600 nm, slit separation 0.2 mm, screen distance 1 m, the fringe width is:
In single-slit diffraction, λ = 500 nm passes through a slit of width 0.1 mm. The angular width of the central maximum is:
Two polarizers are at 60° to each other. Unpolarized light of intensity I₀ is incident on the first. The intensity after the second is:
questions.explanation: After 1st: I₁ = I₀/2. After 2nd: I₂ = I₁cos²60° = (I₀/2)(1/4) = I₀/8.

questions.question: Light travels from glass (n = 1.5) to air. The critical angle is:
A compound microscope has objective f_o = 2 cm, eyepiece f_e = 5 cm. Object at 2.2 cm from objective, image at infinity. The magnifying power is: (D = 25 cm)
questions.explanation: For objective: 1/v_o = 1/f_o + 1/u_o = 1/2 + 1/2.2 → v_o = 22 cm. M_o = v_o/u_o = 10. M_e = D/f_e = 5. Total M = 10 × 5 = 50.

questions.question: In the Compton effect, the change in wavelength of the scattered photon depends on:
options: D) The material of the scatterer
questions.explanation: Compton shift Δλ = (h/m_e c)(1-cosθ), depends only on scattering angle θ.

questions.question: A proton and an electron have the same de Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies K_p/K_e is: (m_p = 1836 m_e)
questions.explanation: λ = h/√(2mK). Same λ → m_pK_p = m_eK_e → K_p/K_e = m_e/m_p = 1/1836.

questions.question: In the Bohr model, the electron in n = 2 orbit of hydrogen has energy:
The wavelength of the first Balmer line (n=3→2) in hydrogen is: (R_H = 1.097×10⁷ m⁻¹)
Binding energy per nucleon for A = 56 is 8.8 MeV. The total binding energy is:
questions.explanation: Total BE = (BE per nucleon) × A = 8.8 × 56 = 492.8 MeV.

A full-wave rectifier using two diodes has ripple frequency for 50 Hz AC input of:
questions.explanation: Full-wave rectifier gives 2 pulses per cycle → ripple = 2×50 = 100 Hz.

questions.question: A Zener diode in a voltage regulator operates in:
questions.explanation: Zener diode operates in reverse bias at breakdown voltage for voltage regulation.

questions.question: In a common-emitter amplifier with β = 100 and base current 10 μA, the collector current is:
The output of a NAND gate with inputs A=1, B=0 is:
questions.explanation: NAND outputs 0 only when all inputs are 1. With A=1, B=0, output is 1.
